newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB to dispose of over Y100 bln in problem loans.
newsitem.headline: LTCB to dispose of over Y100 bln in problem loans.

text.p: Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB), one of Japan's 20 biggest banks, said on Wednesday that it plans to dispose of problem loans of more than 100 billion yen in the fiscal year ending March 1997.
Kazuhiko Oiwa, general manager at LTCB's corporate planning division, told Reuters: "We plan to dispose of problem loans of more than 100 billion yen within the current fiscal year."

He also said the bank expects its earnings for the first half of 1996/97 to be in line with its previous forecast, as neither interest rates nor stock markets moved sufficiently to affect its business forecasts.

In May, LTCB projected parent current profit of 10 billion yen for the first half and 20 billion yen for the full year. It posted a parent current loss of 110.48 billion yen in 1995/96 because it disposed problem loans totalling 650 billion yen, including those to failed housing loan firms.

At the end of March 1996, LTCB had problem loans totalling about 1.2 trillion yen, including those to troubled clients but mainly to its own non-bank affiliates. The problem loans were covered by loan loss provisions totalling 430 billion yen.
Oiwa said the bank expects to establish a trust banking subsidiary in the latter half of 1996/97. He did not elaborate.

LTCB has said since earlier this year that it would reduce its assets by 1.3 trillion yen within the next two years by cutting loan assets by one trillion yen by March 31, 1997 and selling shareholdings worth 300 billion yen by March 31, 1998.
Oiwa said the bank's restructuring programme has begun to contribute to its earnings for the current fiscal year.

He also said that while the bank has focused on reducing less profitable assets and problem loans, it does not plan to raise capital through new share issues at the moment. "We don't have any detailed idea for (equity-linked) financing for now. This is a subject for the future," he said.
